segments.voice: Yesterday's line: outdoors, where the lilies and the signs wait to be read. This week built a day and a week: for the night, my day, rest day, one a week, my people, outdoors. One more weekly piece: a longer reading.

segments.voice: Buying an online course takes a click; finishing it is another matter. Here's a class that held a whole square until noon. In Jerusalem, after the exile, the people gathered as one in the square before the water gate and asked Ezra the scribe to bring out the book of the law. He stood on a wooden platform. When he opened the book, everyone stood up. He read from morning until midday, and they listened the whole time. And then they began to weep.
screen: `SIGN UP, NEVER FINISH.` → `THE SQUARE BY THE WATER GATE.` → `EVERYONE STANDS.` → `THEN THEY WEEP.`

segments.voice: Ezra didn't read alone. Levites stood with the people, and the book of Nehemiah describes what they did: So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading. A reading, and teachers to explain it. Why the tears? The text doesn't say; some readers think the people were hearing how far they had drifted from it. But the leaders stopped them: This day is holy unto the LORD your God; mourn not, nor weep. Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared. And then: the joy of the LORD is your strength. That is the teaching. In Jewish tradition, study is a holy act, and here it ends at a table. Tradition remembers Ezra among those who set the public reading of the Torah, and in synagogues it is read week by week, a portion at a time, the parashah, with teachers who give the sense. Weekly study is that rhythm: a longer reading, someone to explain it, and joy at the end.
screen: `THEY GAVE THE SENSE.` · `MOURN NOT, NOR WEEP.` · `THE JOY OF THE LORD IS YOUR STRENGTH.` · `A PORTION EVERY WEEK.` · then, large: `STUDY.`

segments.voice: Pick up a book you've meant to study, or bring to mind one class you could join. Write on the first page, by hand, the day and hour you'll come back to it each week. Then read its first line once, slowly, and let it settle with your breathing.
Weekly study: a longer reading or a class at a set time each week, with someone who gives the sense, and a little joy at the end.
Pocket this one: study, with the sense given and a table after. Two weeks, built and done.

howItsDone: Jewish communities read the Torah aloud in synagogue on Shabbat, Mondays and Thursdays, a portion (parashah) each week, and study it with teachers and partners.
